title: Pied French Bulldog: Colors, Genetics and Deafness Risk
seoTitle: Pied French Bulldog: Colors, Genetics & Hearing
description: What a pied French Bulldog is, which pied colors the breed standards accept, how the MITF gene works, and why a BAER hearing test matters.

faq.a: No. Pied is a traditional French Bulldog color accepted by the AKC, FCI and Royal Kennel Club standards. A "rare" label on a pied puppy is marketing, not genetics.

faq.q: Are pied French Bulldogs more likely to be deaf?
faq.a: Congenital deafness in dogs is associated with white pigmentation and is most common in dogs with piebald or merle genes. Most pied Frenchies hear normally, but a BAER test is the only way to check each ear.

faq.q: What gene makes a French Bulldog pied?
faq.a: The piebald pattern is linked to a variant in the MITF gene at the S locus. Other white-spotting genes also affect how much white a dog shows, so the DNA test does not predict the exact amount.

faq.q: Is a black and white pied French Bulldog accepted by the AKC?
faq.a: The AKC standard disqualifies "black and white" and "white with black," and says black means black without a trace of brindle. White with brindle patches is accepted, and many dark pieds are actually brindle.

faq.q: What is the difference between pied and merle?
faq.a: Pied is white spotting from the S locus. Merle is a different gene that dilutes pigment in patches and carries higher hearing and eye risks, especially when a dog has two copies.
